summary: Add an isSameOrigin(a, b) helper to ufo, with the semantics agreed first through tests in test/same-origin.test.ts. The tests are drafted with strict port comparison. The helper is not implemented yet.
narrative: On 2026-11-03 the owner asked for an isSameOrigin(a, b) helper in ufo. They wanted the tests written first, in test/same-origin.test.ts, to agree the semantics, and said not to implement it yet. The agent read the isSamePath tests and the origin handling in src/url.ts (obs 2). It then drafted the test spec, leaving open questions as test.todo entries (obs 3). The owner replied that it looked reasonable but wanted ports kept strict: https://example.com and https://example.com:443 must not match, with a case for exactly that. The agent changed the spec to compare ports literally (obs 4). Implementation was deferred to a later session. A different conversation recorded after this (prompt 5, 07:05) has the owner reversing the port rule, so that default ports match. That change is not yet reflected in the tests, so the semantics are still unsettled.

milestones.text: Owner asked for tests-first isSameOrigin(a, b) in test/same-origin.test.ts, with no implementation yet.
Drafted the isSameOrigin test spec, with open questions left as test.todo.
Spec changed to compare ports literally after the owner's correction. Default-port normalization dropped.
Owner, in another conversation, said default ports should now count as the same origin. The tests do not yet reflect this.

preferences.preference: Agree on semantics through tests before any implementation is written.
preferences.quote: Before any implementation, write the test cases in a new test/same-origin.test.ts so we can agree on the semantics. Don't implement it yet.

preferences.preference: Prefer explicit, strict behavior over implicit normalization.
preferences.quote: keep it strict. `https://example.com` and `https://example.com:443` should NOT count as the same origin, I don't want magic port normalization in there.
